justification: New free consumer tool (/tools/upzoning-check): per-address Housing-SEPP form eligibility under the 2025 LMR/TOD reforms. ALL eligibility logic is delegated verbatim to the existing tested engine (services/housing_sepp_eligibility.evaluate_eligibility - live 776/752/759/452 gates, heritage suppression, fail-closed); the new code is a thin exposure layer (FastAPI endpoint + rate-limited Next proxy + page) plus 10 route-level tests that run the REAL engine. Live end-to-end verification against real Portal/ArcGIS/DB ran twice: the first run caught a zone-field mapping bug (fixed + regression-pinned); the second run shows all three archetype addresses correct (Kogarah R4/TOD, Haberfield heritage exclusions, Concord lot-size gates). Also includes a 2-line jest fix for CrossSellCards expectations left stale by the #703 codename rename (pre-existing main breakage).

pre_impl.existing_data: Everything needed already existed and is reused, none re-implemented: resolve_address/get_raw_controls/parse_controls from scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py (the conveyancing pipeline's own address-to-controls path), fetch_lot_geometry/calculate_lot_dimensions from services/lot_dimensions.py, and the whole eligibility engine services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py with its live gate fetchers in services/portal_constraints.py (layers 776/752/759/452, verified live in the 2026-07-13 pre-impl smoke test).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Two assumptions died on contact with reality. (1) The memory note said the eligibility engine was frontend-only with mock station data - stale; the backend engine exists, is tested, and queries live layers. (2) parse_controls field naming: assumed zone_full carried the zone code; it actually carries the portal's zone NAME with no code (generate_conveyancing_report.py:3999), which the live verify exposed when every address came back not_residential - fixed and regression-pinned.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New: services/upzoning_check.py (thin router, no gate or eligibility logic), the /api/upzoning proxy, and the /tools/upzoning-check page. Explicitly NOT reused: app/api/housing-sepp/eligibility/route.ts - it trusts caller-supplied isLMRArea and defaults it TRUE when unspecified (route.ts:198), which is precisely the Haberfield heritage false-positive the smoke test demonstrated; the Python engine is the single safe composition and this endpoint delegates to it.

functions.name: run_upzoning_check
functions.input: UpzoningRequest with a single free-text NSW street address string
functions.output: dict: zone code and name, lot area/frontage, heritage flag plus item names, live gate booleans, status ok|not_residential|unavailable, and forms[] serialized verbatim from FormEligibility
functions.if_none: Unresolvable address or missing coordinates raises HTTPException 422 (blank address 400); every downstream helper failure degrades to None inputs which the engine treats as unconfirmed, never as a passed standard

functions.name: _controls_for
functions.input: Planning Portal property id integer, or None when address resolution produced no id
functions.output: parse_controls dict carrying zone code, zone name, EPI name, legislation url and heritage item/HCA lists
functions.if_none: Missing prop_id or a fetch exception returns parse_controls([]) - the empty-shape dict - so zone stays None and the response degrades to not_residential labelling rather than crashing or fabricating controls

functions.name: _lot_dims
functions.input: Planning Portal property id integer, or None when the address did not resolve to a lot
functions.output: tuple of lot area in square metres and frontage in metres derived from Portal lot geometry
functions.if_none: Any gap (no prop_id, fetch failure, degenerate geometry) returns (None, None); the engine then marks width/area-gated forms unconfirmed and conservatively ineligible, which the page renders as amber not-determinable, never green

values.value: controls zone field (Planning Portal Zone attribute - the zone CODE)
values.read_at: services/upzoning_check.py run_upzoning_check, after the parallel controls fetch
values.if_missing: normalize_zone of an empty value returns empty string, forms come back [], and the response is labelled not_residential - no eligibility is ever asserted without a mapped residential zone code

values.value: gates dict from hse._gate_inputs (live 776/752/759/452 point queries)
values.if_missing: _gate_inputs is fail-closed by design: any gate query failure yields conservative False (never falsely eligible) and the engine reason strings hedge with the area-unconfirmed wording

values.read_at: page.tsx form-card render branch (amber vs green vs grey)
values.if_missing: asdict serialization preserves the field; the page defaults falsy, so an absent flag renders the stricter plain-ineligible state, never an eligible one

queries: N/A - this change adds no SQL. The only DB read is the engine's existing housing_sepp_standards fetch inside housing_sepp_eligibility._fetch_standards_grouped, which is untouched; its failure path is exercised by test_standards_outage_reports_unavailable_not_empty_success.

break_it.scenario: Heritage lot rendered as LMR-eligible (the Haberfield trap: the 776 exclusion layer is sparse and returns nothing on HCA lots, so a zone-plus-776 shortcut says terraces are allowed in a conservation area)
break_it.what_happens: A maximum-liability false positive on a public consumer surface - telling a heritage-land owner they gained development rights they do not have
break_it.how: the endpoint never composes gates itself - it passes the parsed heritage flag into evaluate_eligibility, whose heritage suppression is engine-tested; test_heritage_lot_suppresses_lmr_forms_but_not_base_forms re-asserts it end-to-end at the route with the real engine running, and the live Haberfield run shows the exclusions rendering

break_it.scenario: Standards-table outage renders as an empty-but-successful result, so no housing types shown reads as nothing is possible here
break_it.what_happens: A silent wrong result served during a DB outage - the silent-failure class pre-pr-review rule four exists to catch
break_it.how: evaluate_eligibility returns [] for BOTH non-residential zones and standards failures; the endpoint disambiguates via status ok|not_residential|unavailable and the page renders unavailable as a visible amber outage box stating it is a data outage, not a planning result

break_it.scenario: Unconfirmed lot data (no mappable frontage or area) rendered as a definitive does-not-meet-standards verdict
break_it.what_happens: Grey-as-red: a data gap presented to the user as a failed standard, the Bowral regression class
break_it.how: the engine unconfirmed flag flows through asdict untouched; the page renders unconfirmed forms with an amber not-determinable icon and the engine's own hedged reason wording, visually distinct from both eligible green and failed grey

break_it.scenario: Liability language drift on a free public surface - eligibility framed as advice or an approval outcome
break_it.what_happens: Consumer-law exposure at the same stakes as the paid PDF wording, on an anonymous free page
break_it.how: engine reason strings render verbatim and are never rewritten in TypeScript; all new copy passed the banned-word grep clean; the page carries an explicit not-planning-advice paragraph and frames every result as a mapped-standards screen subject to a development application
break_it.repro: grep -inE the banned-word alternation over the three new files returns nothing

break_it.scenario: Live ArcGIS gate failure silently produces a false eligible (a gate query dies mid-request and the form passes anyway)
break_it.what_happens: A network flake converts into granted development rights shown to an anonymous visitor
break_it.how: gates come exclusively from the engine's own _gate_inputs, fail-closed by design (failure yields conservative False, never falsely eligible); the accepted trade-off is a conservative false negative during outages with hedged wording, never a false positive
break_it.repro: existing tests in tests/test_housing_sepp_eligibility.py pin _gate_inputs fail-safety; the endpoint passes gates through without modification

break_it.scenario: Test fixtures use an idealised field shape that masks a real-data mapping bug - the zone_full fixture embedded the zone code, so normalizing the wrong field still passed every mocked test
break_it.what_happens: All mocked tests green while every real lot is mislabelled not_residential in production - exactly what the first live verify run showed
break_it.how: fixtures corrected to the documented parse_controls shape (zone name WITHOUT code, per generate_conveyancing_report.py:3999); test_zone_code_comes_from_the_zone_field_not_the_name pins the field preference; the live end-to-end re-run against real Portal, ArcGIS and DB is part of the verification record
